overview.description: Bandar Q is a high-speed Indonesian gambling game played with a single set of 28 dominoes. It is a 'banking' game where one player acts as the 'Bandar' (Dealer) and others wager against them. The game's name comes from 'Kiu' (9), the highest possible hand value. Each participant is dealt two dominoes, and the goal is to have a pip total whose units digit is closer to 9 than the Banker's. Famous for its simple 'Modulo-10' math and rapid turnover, it is a staple of Southeast Asian social gambling.
overview.originName: Bandar Q (Indonesian banking domino game named for the 'kiu' or 9 value).

history.origins: Originating in Indonesia as a simplified version of 'Qiu Qiu' (9-9). While Qiu Qiu uses four tiles and is closer to poker, Bandar Q was designed for faster banking action, similar to the western game of Baccarat but using dominoes instead of cards.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Domino cards (made of thick paper) become popular in Southeast Asian ports.
1980s: Bandar Q stabilizes as a distinct casino-style game in underground social dens.
Present: Highly popular in online gaming circles throughout Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.
history.evolution: The game moved from traditional ceramic tiles to printed cards for ease of shuffling in high-turnover gambling environments.
history.cultural: Often played at festivals or community gatherings where the role of 'Bandar' rotates among the wealthiest players.

setup.players: 2-8 players. One is the 'Bandar' (Banker); others are 'Pemasang' (Bettors).
setup.deck: A standard double-six set of 28 dominoes (0-0 to 6-6).
setup.dealing: After bets are placed, each player and the Banker receive 2 tiles face down.

rules.objective: Score a total closer to 9 than the Banker to win your bet.
rules.gameplay: Bettors place wagers. Each player and the Banker receive two dominoes. Pip total modulo 10; closest to 9 wins. Banker wins ties.
keyRules: The Banker always wins on a tie.
A hand of 10 pips is 0 points (the 'Baccarat' equivalent of the game).

strategy.basic: As a bettor, manage your bankroll. Since the Banker has a statistical edge (winning on ties), avoid max-betting on every hand.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Switch' Strategem: In social games where the Banker role is optional, only accept the role if you have a sufficient bankroll to cover multiple 'Kiu' double-payouts.
strategy.advanced: Statistical Tracking: In a 28-tile game with 8 players, 16 tiles are in play. If you have seen many high tiles such as 6-6 and 5-6 in previous rounds and the deck is not shuffled every turn, the probability of low hands increases.
tips: Winning with a 9 is the only way to get a double payout. It's the 'Jackpot' of the game.
If you are the Banker, a 9 is your best defense, as it takes all bets and negates any player 9s.

difficulty.easy: Makes random bet sizes. Doesn't understand the Banker's tie advantage.
difficulty.medium: Varies bet size based on previous wins. Prefers being the Banker when the bankroll allows.
difficulty.hard: Optimal bankroll management using the Kelly Criterion. Calculates the 'Kiu' probability based on the remaining 28 tiles if playing in a session with partial deck consumption.

considerations: AI must handle the 'Banker' role transition logic.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 28-tile double-six domino set. Each tile has two ends showing zero to six pips; every combination from 0-0 through 6-6 appears exactly once. No playing cards; used for Bandar Q and similar domino banking games.
engine.suitDescription: Tiles are matched by pip value at the open ends of the layout. There are no traditional suits; each end value zero through six can connect to any tile sharing that value on one of its two ends.
engine.rankDescription: There is no rank hierarchy between tiles; play legality is determined by matching the pip value at an open end. Doubles (same pips on both ends) may have special rules. Scoring follows the game.
